# Page 5^page=5
Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Internal Ombudsman) Directions, 2026 These Directions shall be applicable to Commercial Banks (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'banks' and individually as a 'bank') having 10 or more banking outlets in India as on March 31, 2025, whether such bank is incorporated in India or outside India. The directions shall also be applicable to the commercial bank, which meets the above mentioned criteria after March 31, 2025, with effect from six months from meeting the eligibility criteria.

# Page 6^page=6
Appointment of Internal Ombudsman The IO shall either be a retired or serving officer, in the rank equivalent to a General Manager in the RE under the purview of the Internal Ombudsman framework or a Financial Sector Regulatory Body, having necessary skills and experience of minimum seven years of working in areas such as banking, non-banking finance, regulation, supervision, payment and settlement systems, credit information or consumer protection. The IO shall previously not have been employed, nor presently be employed, by the bank or a holding, associate or subsidiary company of the bank. The IO shall not be over 70 years of age before the completion of the tenure. A person may work as the IO in more than one RE simultaneously at the discretion of the REs concerned, subject to the approval of the Board or Customer Service Committee / Consumer Protection Committee of the Board of the appointing RE. Must relinquish current post before assuming charge as IO

# Page 7^page=7
Appointment of Deputy Internal Ombudsman The Dy. IO shall either be a retired or serving officer, in the rank equivalent to a Deputy General Manager in the RE under the purview of the Internal Ombudsman framework or a Financial Sector Regulatory Body, having necessary skills and experience of minimum five years of working in areas such as banking, non-banking finance, regulation, supervision, payment and settlement systems, credit information or consumer protection. The Dy. IO shall previously not have been employed, nor presently be employed, by the bank or a holding, associate or subsidiary company of the bank. The Dy. IO shall not be over 70 years of age before the completion of the tenure. The Dy. IO shall not be employed in more than one RE simultaneously.

# Page 8^page=8
Number of Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman Every bank shall appoint at least one IO. The CSC of the Board shall determine, at least once in a year, the number of IO/ Dy. IO to be appointed having due regard to volume and complexity of the complaints received, and ensuring that the IO/ Dy. IO get sufficient time to apply his/her mind on the principles of fairness, equity and natural justice while reviewing the resolution provided by the bank. While appointing additional IO / Dy. IO, the bank shall consider the need for diversity of experience of the incumbents to deal with different types of cases. In such cases, the bank may clearly define the jurisdiction of each IO / Dy. IO. The IO shall report to the Competent Authority (Whole Time Director / Executive Director in- charge of customer service vertical of the bank), and to the CSC of the Board of the bank functionally.

# Page 9^page=9
Tenure of Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman The bank must ensure that the post of IO is never vacant. During temporary absence of the IO, the Dy. IO shall function as IO. If both IO and Dy. IO are absent, the bank may designate a serving officer of GM rank as IO for a maximum period of one month, with approval of the Customer Service Committee (CSC) of the Board, and such officer must have no reporting relationship with business verticals during this period. The tenure shall be a fixed term of at least 3 years, and the maximum total tenure (including extension/reappointment) shall not exceed 5 years. The bank must initiate the fresh appointment process at least 3 months before expiry of the tenure and ensure a reasonable overlap between outgoing and incoming IO. The IO / Dy. IO cannot be removed before completion of tenure without CSC approval. In case of vacancy due to unavoidable reasons, the bank shall inform RBI within 10 working days and appoint a new IO / Dy. IO within 3 months from the date of vacancy. The CSC of the Board of the bank shall determine the structure of emoluments, facilities and benefits accorded to the IO / Dy.

# Page 10^page=10
Role and Responsibilities of Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman The office of the IO shall not handle complaints received directly from the complainants or members of the public. It shall deal with the complaints that have already been examined by the bank but have been partially resolved or being wholly rejected by the bank. While the IO may decide any or all complaints, the power for the Dy. IO to decide the complaints may be defined under a policy approved by the Customer Service Committee of the Board. The IO / Dy. IO may recommend compensation to the complainant in line with RBI’s extant compensation guidelines, or as per the bank’s compensation policy where RBI guidelines are not specified. The IO may recommend additional compensation as per the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme for consequential loss, loss of time, expenses incurred, and harassment or mental agony, over and above the basic compensation.

# Page 11^page=11
Role and Responsibilities of Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman The office of the IO shall conduct quarterly analysis of complaints, including product- wise, category-wise, consumer group-wise and region-wise patterns, and provide inputs for policy-level interventions. The IO / Dy. IO shall have read-only access to the RBI’s Complaint Management System, enabling them to stay informed about decisions of the RBI Ombudsman. The bank shall seek such access for the IO / Dy. IO from the Consumer Education and Protection Department of the Reserve Bank. The Dy. IO shall functionally report to the IO.

# Page 12^page=12
Procedure for Complaint Redress by Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman Banks shall implement a fully automated Complaint Management System (CMS) with access provided to the IO / Dy. IO. All partially resolved or wholly rejected complaints shall be auto-escalated to the IO: ▪ At least 10 days for review of such complaints in cases where RBI / NPCI / card networks prescribe resolution timelines, and ▪ Within 20 days of receipt in all other cases. The CMS shall classify complaints only as Fully Resolved, Partially Resolved, or Wholly Rejected, except for complaints outside the IO’s purview. Complaints outside the IO’s purview include: • Complaints related to corporate frauds, misappropriation etc.not impacting customers, • Suggestions and commercial decisions (except service deficiencies), • Internal administration, HR, and staff remuneration matters, • Matters pending or decided by judicial/quasi-judicial bodies, and • Disputes for which remedy has been provided under CIC (Regulation) Act, 2005 Rejected/partially resolved complaints under corporate frauds and commercial decisions shall still be forwarded to the IO to examine service deficiency, and those outside scope shall be returned to the bank.

# Page 13^page=13
Procedure for Complaint Redress by Internal Ombudsman / Deputy Internal Ombudsman The bank shall ensure that the final decision is communicated to the complainant within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of complaint by the bank A complaint shall not be closed by the same branch or unit; partially resolved or rejected complaints must be reviewed at a senior level before being sent to the IO. The IO / Dy. IO shall examine complaints based on bank records, may seek additional documents, interact with bank officials, and, if required, obtain written or oral submissions from the complainant. Where the IO / Dy. IO upholds the decision of the bank to reject or partially resolve the complaint, the reply to the complainant should explicitly state that the said complaint has been reviewed by the IO / Dy. IO. The IO / Dy. IO shall record a “reasoned decision” in each case. For complaints that are partially resolved or wholly rejected after examination by the IO / Dy. IO, the bank shall advise the complainant about the option of approaching the RBI Ombudsman for redress. The bank in its reply shall also mention the URL of Reserve Bank’s CMS portal for online filing of customer complaints and the physical / email address of the CRPC.

# Page 14^page=14
Additional Information The bank shall, within five working days of appointment of the IO or Dy. IO, furnish the details of the official so appointed to the Consumer Education and Protection Department, Central Office, Reserve Bank of India. The bank shall put in place a system for periodic Report on functioning of IO to the Consumer Education and Protection Department, RBI, on a quarterly basis. The report shall be submitted on or before the 15th day of the month following the quarter to which it relates to. The Internal Audit Department of the bank shall conduct an audit of the implementation of these Directions on an annual basis. The office of the IO may preferably be placed in the Head Office or Corporate Office of the bank. The IO shall be designated as a permanent invitee to the meetings of the CSC of the Board. The IO shall furnish periodic reports (including the analysis of complaints) on his / her activities to the CSC of the Board, preferably at quarterly, but not less than half yearly, intervals. The decision of the IO / Dy. IO can be overruled only with the approval of the Competent Authority and shall be placed before the CSC for review. An analysis of the top five complaint categories and the remedial measures taken to prevent recurrence shall be placed before CSC of the board on the quarterly basis.

# Page 15^page=15
Additional Information ▪ These Directions shall be applicable to Small Finance Banks having 10 or more banking outlets in India as on March 31, 2025. ▪ These Directions shall be applicable to Payments Banks having 10 or more banking outlets in India as on March 31, 2025. ▪ These directions shall be applicable to NBFCs (excluding Housing Finance Company, Core Investment Company, Infrastructure Debt Fund-Non-Banking Financial Company, Non-Banking Financial Company - Infrastructure Finance Company, Non-Operative Financial Holding Company, Primary dealers, Mortgage Guarantee Company) fulfilling the following criteria as on March 31, 2025: o Deposit-taking NBFCs (NBFCs-D) with 10 or more branches; o Non-Deposit taking NBFCs (NBFCs-ND) with asset size of Rs.5,000 crore and above and having public customer interface; ▪ These Directions shall be applicable to Non-Bank Prepaid Payment Instruments Issuers and having more than one crore Prepaid Payment Instruments outstanding as on March 31, 2025, or thereafter. ▪ The provisions of these Directions shall be applicable to Credit Information Companies

# Page 16^page=16
Q.1) As per the Internal Ombudsman framework, which of the following correctly describes the eligibility and appointment conditions of an Internal Ombudsman (IO)? (a) The IO must be a serving officer of the bank at the rank of General Manager and should have at least five years’ experience in banking or finance. (b) The IO can be a retired or serving officer equivalent to General Manager level, with a minimum of seven years’ experience in banking, NBFCs or regulation, but may be employed by the bank’s subsidiary. (c) The IO must be a retired officer of a financial institution, below the rank of General Manager, with ten years’ experience, and shall not serve if more than fifty years at the time of selection. (d) The IO may be a retired or serving GM-equivalent officer with seven years’ relevant experience, below seventy years at tenure completion, and permitted to serve multiple REs with Board/CSC approval. (e) The IO must be appointed exclusively from among retired RBI officers and shall not be permitted to work for any other Regulated Entity. Answer: ?

(a) 5 ; 1,000 (b) 10 ; 2,000 (c) 10 ; 5,000 (d) 15 ; 10,000 (e) 20 ; 5,000 Answer: ?
